New BMW M350 xDrive Gets a Virtual Tuning Job, Do You Dig the Sportier Design?
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | a.c.g_design
BMW has an entirely new 3 Series in its portfolio, the G50. The model debuted almost one month ago, and has yet to hit the assembly line, as the production is scheduled to commence in 2027 at the Dingolfing factory in Germany.
Therefore, we can say that the paint has barely dried on its body, yet it seems that a good chunk of the tuning world (and not only) already wants a piece of the action. That’s understandable, given that the petrolhead crowd has big expectations from this model, and while you are reading these lines, chances are your favorite tuner is already deciding what to cook up for the sports sedan in order to make it cool.
I would have said “more cool” instead of “cool,” but in my opinion, there is nothing “cool” about the new-generation BMW 3 Series . Well, other than the platform, because it is based on an updated version of the old CLAR architecture. This means that despite venturing into the Neue Klasse era both inside and out, it still shares its nuts and bolts not only with its predecessor, the G2X, but also the G3X 5 Series, the G32 6 Series, G01 X3, G02 X4, G2X 4 Series, the usual M models, the demised Z4, and the Toyota GR Supra.
So, why is it not cool in my vision? Because the Neue Klasse design does not do justice to this otherwise iconic model. The vizor-like face makes it look like a mainstream model, perhaps one made by a Chinese brand, and the back end is definitely on the quirky side of things, too. And then comes the interior, with its tech-filled nature, which will likely age like a smartphone to the point where not many gearheads would want a used G5X 3er a few years from now.
Photo: Instagram | a.c.g_design The same will also apply to its range-topping sibling, the new-gen BMW M3 , which is reportedly due in 2028, some one year after the mechanically-unrelated M3 Electric launches. The ICE M3 will feature some M Concept Neue Klasse-inspired design cues, a similar interior with the usual M touches, a dedicated chassis setup, uprated brakes, and a 3.0-liter twin-turbo straight-six, likely with MHEV assistance, that could offer north of 600 hp.
Meanwhile, if you want a fast new-gen 3er, then you will have to settle for the new BMW M350 xDrive. And it is this exact model that has recently fallen into the hands of the rendering crowd, as a small chunk of its has imagined what this thing would look like if it were visited by the tuning fairy. The same goes for @a.c.g_design on Instagram, which signed the digital illustrations shared in the gallery above, and would want to know what you think of it.
This virtually-tuned BMW M350 xDrive features a new hood, a tweaked bumper at the front with an apron attached to it, side skirt extensions, and dedicated trim on the front fenders. Out back, it is home to a new diffuser with an extra brake light in the middle, close to the OEM bumper, a double bubble-like ducktail spoiler, and a wing. The Y-spoke concave wheels with their silver finish are new, the car rides closer to the ground, and features a blue look on the outside, complete with some black elements, and tinted windows all around.
Photo: Instagram | a.c.g_design Quite strangely, there are no yellow daytime running lights on deck, and in case you forgot, these will be a thing for this version of the new-generation BMW 3 Series. The M350 xDrive has 437 bhp to play with, which equals 325 kilowatts and 443 metric horsepower, and the 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged straight-six engine with 48-volt mild-hybrid assistance develops 428 pound-feet (580 Nm) of torque, the model’s spec sheet reveals.
Channeling the output and thrust to the rear-biased xDrive all-wheel drive system is an eight-speed automatic transmission. BMW’s new M350 xDrive takes 3.9 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill, which makes it 0.2 seconds faster than the current M3 Sedan, aka the base one. The M3 Competition Sedan, which has a bit more oomph (503 instead of 473 brake horsepower), hits 60 mph in 3.8 seconds, and the M3 Competition xDrive Sedan, with its 523 bhp, will complete the sprint in 3.4 seconds.
Ordering the new BMW M350 xDrive with sport tires means that this model will eventually run out of breath at 155 mph (250 kph), and the top speed is 130 mph (210 kph) without this option. And we cannot wait to see how fast the next-generation BMW M3 is, and how much power it has, though it is logical to assume that it will offer more than 600 hp in order to be on par with Audi Sport’s new RS 5 and Mercedes-AMG’s C 63.
Now, what’s your take on this virtually-tuned new-gen BMW 3 Series ? Is the CGI makeover a yay or a nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Λutomotive Custom Garage (@a.c.g_design)
